newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo state closer to privatization bond offer.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo state closer to privatization bond offer.

text.p: Sao Paulo's state government next week will create an asset management company that will one day offer privatization bonds in exchange for state debt, said an official at the Sao Paulo Energy Secretariat.

The Sao Paulo State Asset Management Company (CPA) will have an initial social capital of 6.7 billion reais ($6.5 billion), which could be increased to 15 billion reais, depending on government needs, said Ricardo Lima, an official at the secretariat who advises investors on the state's privitization plan.
Under the state's privatization law, investors must use privatization bonds to pay for at least 30 percent of a state firm at auction, he said.
The government does not know yet when it is going to offer the privatization bonds because the state is still consolidating its massive debt.
The maximum amount of privatization bonds that can be used to buy state assets will be defined later by consultants, who are to be hired by the government during the privatization process, Lima said.
